reasons: The cited text (Section 7.7) plainly imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer at 15% of annual Fees per week, so 'deviation' is correctly classified under rule LD (flag only when Customer pays).

The redline reaches the preferred position by removing the Customer-payable liquidated damages entirely and substituting a conventional, non-punitive late-payment interest charge capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum; the 10-day trigger and surrounding payment mechanics are preserved.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (ratio 1.042) is explained by the rule itself: the operative sentence is the liquidated-damages obligation, so replacing it wholesale is the smallest edit that achieves the playbook position; no unrelated terms were touched.

The comment is accurate, correctly states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and reasonably explains why the 3-month early-termination fallback is inapplicable (no termination fee in the clause at issue).

Minor point for negotiation awareness only, not a defect: the added 'Vendor's sole remedy' framing goes slightly beyond deleting the LD by potentially foreclosing suspension/termination for non-payment, and the reference to 'Applicable Law' as defined at Section 1.2 is not verifiable from the supplied definitions — confirm the defined term exists or use plain language.
